title: Word 5 — On Our Renewal by Holy Baptism
attribution_note: Word 5 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: In holy Baptism, Christian, we are renewed unto a holy, Christian, new life; and putting off the old man, we are clothed in the new, spiritual man, and, laying aside the ill-nature of the old Adam, we receive the good nature of the new Adam, Jesus Christ, and thus become a new creature, according to the apostolic teaching: *“If any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”* [2 Corinthians 5:17]. Therefore holy Baptism is called the washing of regeneration [Titus 3:5]. For before Baptism we were dead, having died through sin, and capable of no good work — for what can a dead man do? — and so we were before God as though we did not exist, for in God's sight only he is alive who is dead to sin. But in holy Baptism we are quickened by the grace of God, and, having renounced sin, are renewed unto a holy and godly life.

Every Christian has, as it were, two births: the old, that is, the fleshly, and the new, that is, the spiritual. The old birth he has from his parents: and he is conceived in iniquities and born in sins [Psalm 50:7]. The second, spiritual birth he has as well, and through it he is regenerated unto a spiritual, holy and heavenly life, and this life he receives from Christ — and for this he is called a Christian, for a man is named after him from whom he is born.

sections.heading: What the flesh bequeaths, what the Spirit gives

pairs.en: In our fleshly birth we inherit pride, high-mindedness, haughtiness, arrogance, self-conceit, and contempt for our neighbor; but with the spiritual birth are joined humility, self-abasement and self-contempt.
In the fleshly birth we receive unbelief, but in the spiritual, faith.
In the fleshly birth we inherit fearlessness, but in the spiritual, the fear of God.
With the fleshly birth are joined disobedience, unruliness, insubordination and resistance to God, but with the spiritual, obedience, submission and compliance.
To the fleshly birth belongs ingratitude, but to the spiritual, thankfulness to God.
To the fleshly belongs negligence of God's honor and glory, but to the spiritual, zeal and concern for God's glory.
In the fleshly birth we inherit hope in ourselves — in our own honor, wealth, and strength, in man and every created thing — but in the spiritual birth there arises hope in God alone.

sections.heading: From wrath to love, from deceit to truth

pairs.en: In the fleshly birth we acquire anger, rage, malice, and the desire to avenge ourselves in word and deed; but with the spiritual birth are joined meekness, freedom from malice, and long-suffering.
In the fleshly birth we receive immoderate self-love, but to the spiritual birth belong love of God and love of man.
To the fleshly belongs stinginess, love of money, mercilessness and concern only for oneself, but to the spiritual, mercy, generosity, compassion, and a desire to help one's neighbor.
With the fleshly is joined envy and all the evil that flows from it, but with the spiritual, love, and compassion for a neighbor's misfortune, and joy at his happiness.
With the fleshly are joined flattery, cunning, lying, craftiness and hypocrisy, but with the spiritual, simplicity of heart and truth.
With the fleshly go plunder, theft and every kind of unrighteousness, but with the spiritual, righteousness.
With the fleshly go impurity, incontinence, and the lust of fornication, but with the spiritual, purity, chastity and self-restraint.

In the fleshly birth we inherit love of this world, that is, *“the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life”* [1 John 2:16] — in other words, the fleshly mind; but in the spiritual birth we acquire contempt for this world and all its vanity, and the spiritual mind, that is, a striving toward heavenly and eternal blessings.
In a word, to the fleshly birth belongs ill-nature, and to the spiritual, good nature.

sections.heading: Showing the fruits of the new birth

pairs.en: Here, then, we see what the fruits of the fleshly birth are, and what the fruits of the spiritual birth are. When holy Scripture commands us to flee from sin, it commands us to flee from the fruits of the old, that is, the fleshly birth; and when it teaches us to do good, it teaches us to show forth the fruits of the new birth. *“Depart from evil, and do good”* [Psalm 33:15]. *“Let every one that nameth the name of the Lord depart from iniquity”* [2 Timothy 2:19].

Beloved Christians! We, thanks be to God, have been born anew and renewed in holy Baptism, as was said above. Let us then examine ourselves — do we show the fruits of the new birth? Do we live as the new birth demands? For a birth cannot be something dead, but must be living, and so it must show forth fruits proper to itself. Let us then show forth the fruits of our new birth, that we may not appear fruitless before our Lord, and hear His dread word: *“I know you not”* [Matthew 25:12].
